text:
ethan.sales: Hey team quick one  booked a multi-city trip on the corporate card (Paris -> Amsterdam -> Munich). The Paris hotel was non-refundable; meeting moved so we canceled Paris and got a partial refund but the hotel kept a 120 fee. Also the Amsterdam night was moved to a colleague's card and she asked me to submit our shared-room split. How do I expense the cancellation fee + split the room + account for the refund on the corp card?

marie.peopleops: Short version: cancellation fees that are business-related and unavoidable (meeting change) are reimbursable. For the corporate card refund, Finance will net the refund against the card activity; you should still submit the cancellation fee as an expense with supporting docs and manager approval. For the shared room, submit the split with both names and attach the original folio showing both guests if available.

dan.finance: Finance details: upload the hotel folio, cancellation policy screenshot, and the refund confirmation email showing net amount charged. Category: Travel > Lodging. For corporate card refunds: we reconcile on the card statement; if you prepaid on a personal card and later got a refund to the same card, show the net charge. If refund went to corp card, you don't need a separate negative expense  Finance will pick it up during reconciliation.

ethan.sales: The refund posted as a single credit to the corp card but the cancellation fee wasn't broken out on the folio  how should I show the 120 fee?

marie.peopleops: If the supplier doesn't break it out, provide the cancellation confirmation email that states the retained amount and the refund amount, plus the corp card statement line. In your expense notes use a pro-rata explanation: e.g., "Room reserved 3 nights, 1 night canceled; hotel retained 120 cancellation fee per confirmation." Manager approval required.

dan.finance: We'll accept the supplier confirmation + card statement as proof for the retained fee. If the supplier can't provide a written confirmation, tag your manager and include a screenshot of the reservation showing non-refundable terms. For amounts > 200 Finance may request supplemental approval.

ethan.sales: About the shared room  colleague Julie paid the Amsterdam night on her personal card. We split 50/50. I have Julie's receipt plus the hotel folio that lists both our names but her receipt shows her charged 160. Should I submit 80 and include her receipt?

marie.peopleops: Yes  submit your half (80) as a reimbursement with Julie's receipt attached as evidence of total paid and the folio showing both guests. Add a short note: "shared room with Julie @julie.sales; reimbursing my 50% (80)." Manager approval required for peer-to-peer splits.

dan.finance: If Julie wants the company to reimburse directly to her, she can submit the full 160 and add a note that Ethan reimbursed her 80 personally. Finance prefers the person who actually paid to claim the full amount and then have internal settlement between employees recorded. The net effect is the same but documentation should be clear.

ethan.sales: Also curious about VAT reclaim: the Paris hotel shows VAT on the folio but the booking was through a consumer OTA for Amsterdam  folio shows no VAT. What do we do for reclaim?

dan.finance: VAT reclaim requires supplier invoice with VAT ID and tax breakdown. For Paris hotel with a proper folio, attach it and we'll attempt reclaim. For OTA bookings without supplier tax data, VAT reclaim is generally not possible. If reclaimability is important for future trips, book directly with supplier or request an invoice at check-in.

marie.peopleops: Reminder on lodging cap: standard corporate lodging cap is 220/night in these regions. If you exceeded cap (e.g., Paris full-rate), please include a brief business justification and manager sign-off for exceptions (client event, safety, peak pricing).

ethan.sales: The Paris rate was 320/night originally  that's why I booked via corporate card. Meeting moved so fee kept. Should I seek exception approval retroactively?

dan.finance: Exceptions should be pre-approved when possible. Retro approvals are allowed but require manager + finance sign-off. Submit the justification: client event pricing and no suitable alternatives. Finance flags exceptions in quarterly audits.

expense-bot: Reminder: tag cost_center and project_code. Use the Travel template. Missing approver will route the expense back. For corp-card reconciliations, attach card statement lines.

ethan.sales: One last nuance  partial-day per-diem for travel day where I had a working dinner paid by client. Can I still claim per-diem?

marie.peopleops: Per-diem rules: you can claim per-diem unless a meal was provided by the client or vendor. If client-paid meal occurred, reduce per-diem by the meal value or mark that meal as covered. Small incidental items (coffee) don't require reductions. Include a note: "client-hosted dinner on travel day; deduct dinner value from per-diem."

dan.finance: If you prefer, itemize the client meal and submit the per-diem reduced accordingly. Either approach is fine; manager approval required for any reduced per-diem logic if unusual.

ethan.sales: Thanks, uploading docs now. Can you paste a sample note I can use?

dan.finance: Sample note to paste into expense (edit dates/amounts):
```
Multi-city client trip 2026-06-02 -> 2026-06-06 (Paris -> Amsterdam -> Munich).
- Paris hotel (non-refundable): original charge \u20ac960 (3 nights). Refund issued \u20ac840. Hotel retained cancellation fee \u20ac120 per confirmation (attached). Manager @sarah.sales approved cancellation policy exception 2026-05-20.
- Amsterdam hotel: total charged \u20ac160 (Julie @julie.sales paid on personal card). Reimbursing my 50% = \u20ac80. Hotel folio with both names attached.
- Per-diem: standard daily per-diem \u20ac50/day. Client-hosted dinner on 2026-06-03 (value \u20ac40)  deduct from per-diem.
Refund credited to corporate card; Finance will reconcile credit. VAT invoice for Paris attached for possible reclaim. Cost_center: SALES-EU; Project_code: PROJ-1234.
```

ethan.sales: Pasted and submitted. Appreciate the clear process. :thumbsup:
